I am trying to find which of the sum of the number of regionally elevated genes in the forebrain of human, pig, and mouse is the largest.

The number of regional elevated genes in human cebral cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus, and hypothalamus is 180, 83, 57,and 110.

The number of regional elevated genes in pig cebral cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus, and hypothalamus is 109, 157, 31,and 45.


The number of regional elevated genes in mouse cebral cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus, and hypothalamus is 55, 185, 60,and 98.

```{r}
human_elevated<-sum(180,83,57,110)
pig_elevated<-sum(109,157,31,45)
mouse_elevated<-sum(55,185,60,98)

print(human_elevated)
print(pig_elevated)
print(mouse_elevated)
```
Therefore, human has the highest number of genes with regionally elevated expression.
